..
Issued at 1254 PM CDT Sat Oct 17 2026

Northwest flow continues aloft as a ridge remains over the region 
through this evening with 850mb winds out of the southwest with the 
highest speeds of 25-35kts over the James Valley and eastward. This 
along with steeper pressure gradients, a southwesterly surface wind 
within a shallow mixing layer under a strong inversion just off the 
surface has led to gusty downsloping winds along the eastern slopes 
of the Coteau. Peak gusts have ranged from 40 to 60 mph over this
area with the highest gust in Peever earlier this morning. 
Through the rest of the afternoon and evening winds will remain 
breezy with this setup James Valley and eastward with gusts of 
25 to 50 mph, with the highest gusts of 40 to 50 mph along the 
eastern slopes of the Coteau. Winds over and along the Coteau 
will diminish a bit this evening before strengthening again late
tonight and overnight as the inversion becomes stronger and 
warmer. For example Peever soundings warms to +22C at 950mb 
around 06Z! HREF ensemble does indicate gusts of 40 to 
potentially 50 mph with winds diminishing through Sunday 
morning. Probability of wind gusts>45 mph tops out at 80% 
between 00Z-06Z or so. Prob of gusts>50 mph is 45-60%. However, 
REFs and NBM are much lower with a prob of winds>45 mph up to 
about 50% REFS and less than 20% NBM, so this leads to lower 
confidence in maximum wind gusts. HRRR Peever sounding shows the
top of the momentum transfer (again right off the ground due to
strong inversion) about 20-25kts and around 15kts per RAP 
overnight. Went ahead and used HRRR from 00-12Z Sunday to show 
for potential higher gusts. Wind gusts will need to be monitored
later on this evening and tonight. 

With this ridge overhead and high pressure so the south and 
southeast, models continue to indicate very dry air over the region 
with RAP 1000-500mb RH below 20% into tonight! This ridge will 
track eastward this evening as a shortwave, and its surface low 
strengthen, as it tracks eastward across central Canada. By 12Z 
Sunday, models indicate the center of the ~984mb low is forecast
to be over northern Manitoba with its cold front extending 
southward over east central ND through central SD. As the front 
tracks southeastward, winds will continue to shift out of the 
northwest behind it, then north/northeast, across the CWA with 
the region behind the cold front by late Sunday afternoon. 
Again, with the ongoing dry air over the region no precipitation
is expected with this fropa passage. Otherwise, high pressure 
moves in behind it through Monday.

With this return flow tonight, overnight temps will be warmer 
ranging in the 40s. Highs for Sunday will be a few degrees cooler 
mainly along and west of the Mo River behind the fropa with highs in 
the upper 60s. While east of the River temps will be able to warm up 
with temps similar to today or a few degrees warmer with highs in 
the mid to upper 60s to around 70 with the warmest temps far 
NESD/western MN. With high pressure moving in and light northeast 
winds, temps will drop into the upper 30s to the lower to mid 40s, 
coldest over north central SD and warmest over the Coteau per 
inversion. This results in the potential for patchy frost over 
portions of north central SD late Sunday night into early Monday 
morning. Temps will remain cooler (still above average) with overall 
highs in the upper 50s to the lower 60s per high over the region 
Monday. 

Looking ahead Tuesday through the end of next week, a -PNA pattern 
sets up with a broad ridge east of the Rockies which results in 
overall dry conditions and temperatures above average. Confidence is 
increasing for precipitation to move back in towards the end of next 
week as Clusters are in agreement on a mid level closed low moving 
in off the southern CA coast and a weaker open wave over the 
northern Pacific/western Canada as they potentially phase together 
into an open wave and tracking east/northeast into the central and 
northern CONUS. Beyond Day 5, there are differences between the 
ensembles on exact placement and intensity of the wave resulting in 
a difference in QPF placement and timing. With this setup, the 
Climate Prediction Center indicates a 50 to 65% chance of above 
normal precipitation 10/22 to 10/26. During this time, there is a 65-
75% chance of above normal temperatures resulting in ptype to stay 
as rain as temps are forecast to range in the 60s and 70s before 
cooler air moves in behind the system next weekend.
